output.title: Know the demo limit before you automate
output.body:
If you have tried ChatGPT but have not connected it to a real workflow, the first question is not whether AI can answer a prompt. It is whether it fits one recurring task in your business without creating a bigger manual job around it.

For a small business, the best candidate is usually a frequent, repeatable workflow with a measurable outcome, already living in English, email, docs, or SaaS tools. That might be customer questions, lead follow-up, or invoice checking. The 8–10 hours a week example is just a persona frame, not a claim about your business.

That is where demo limits matter. Our self-built knowledge assistant is a local demo on synthetic Acme Shop data and approved documents; it can work end to end locally, but the public route is locked. Our accounts-payable demo uses entirely synthetic data for a fictional manufacturer; duplicate-invoice blocking, amount-based human-only approval, and audit records work, while OCR, billing, and multi-user operation do not. The blocked payment demo is simulated, not a real transfer. Money still needs a person in the chair.

The practical next step is simple: pick one recurring workflow and ask whether the output is measurable, the data is already digital, and a human can approve the risky part. If that is still unclear, the workflow is probably too messy for automation yet. If it is clear, that is the boundary worth testing.
